messages.content: Draft me wills for as I have 10 million 3 real estate propertie with 2 children after my wife they will have the nomeny

I don't have enough context to draft a valid UAE will for you. To prepare a compliant will under **Law No. (15) of 2017 on the Regulation of Inheritance, Wills, and Probate Registry in the Emirate of Dubai** and the **Federal Decree-Law No. (5) of 1985 on the Issuance of the Civil Transactions Law of the UAE**, I need the following information:

---

## What I Need From You to Draft a Valid Will

- **Your full name, date of birth, nationality, and Emirates ID/passport number**
- **Your marital status and your wife’s full details** (name, date of birth, nationality, Emirates ID/passport number)
- **Your two children’s full details** (names, dates of birth, nationalities, Emirates IDs/passport numbers)
- **Guardianship arrangements** for your children if they are minors (name and details of the proposed guardian and alternate guardian)
- **Location of your assets**:
  - Are the three real estate properties located in **Dubai**? If so, are they registered under your name or a company?
  - Are there any other assets (bank accounts, investments, vehicles, etc.)?
- **Ownership structure** of the properties (direct ownership, through a company, joint ownership, etc.)
- **Any mortgages, loans, or encumbrances** on the properties
- **Your religion** (to confirm applicability of Law No. (15) of 2017)
- **Whether you want to register the will** with the **Dubai Courts’ Wills Service Centre (DIFC Wills & Probate Registry)** or another competent court
- **Any specific conditions** you want to include (e.g., age of inheritance, education funds, trusts)
- **Any debts or obligations** that must be settled from the estate
- **Whether you want to exclude any legal heirs** (e.g., parents, siblings)

> **Pro-Tip:** Under **Article (4)(c)** of Law No. (15) of 2017, if you have multiple nationalities, you must specify which nationality governs your will upon registration. If you do not specify, the law of your residence or business location will apply.

---

## Overview of UAE Wills for Non-Muslims

Under **Law No. (15) of 2017**, non-Muslims in Dubai (and other emirates that recognize it) can register a **testamentary will** to govern the distribution of their estate, including real estate, bank accounts, and other assets. This law allows you to override **intestate succession** under the **Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. (5) of 1985)**.

Key points:
- A will **takes precedence over intestate succession** ([Article (5)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_3)).
- The will must be **registered** with the **Competent Court** (e.g., Dubai Courts’ Wills Service Centre) to be enforceable.
- The **Executor** (or Administrator) must be appointed and meet legal requirements ([Article (14)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_7)).
- **Debts and funeral expenses** must be settled before distribution ([Article (5)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_3)).
- **Minor children** require a **guardian** and **trustee** (if applicable).

---

## General Structure of a Will Under UAE Law (Explanatory Draft)

> ⚠️ **This is a general explanatory outline only. It is not a final legal document.** You must consult a licensed UAE wills drafting professional to finalize your will.

### ### 1. **Introductory Clause**
- Your full name, date of birth, nationality, and Emirates ID/passport number
- Declaration that you are of sound mind and making the will voluntarily
- Statement that this will revokes all prior wills

### ### 2. **Appointment of Executor**
- Name and details of the **Executor** (must meet requirements under [Article (14)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_7)):
  - Full capacity
  - Not convicted of a felony or crime affecting honour/trustworthiness (unless rehabilitated)
  - Not bankrupt or insolvent (unless rehabilitated)
  - No interest in the willed property
- Alternate Executor (if applicable)

### ### 3. **Appointment of Guardian for Minor Children**
- Name and details of the **guardian** for your children (if they are minors)
- Name and details of the **alternate guardian**
- Powers granted to the guardian (e.g., education, maintenance, housing)

### ### 4. **Distribution of Estate**
- **Real estate properties**: List each property with full address and title deed details
- **Other assets**: Bank accounts, investments, vehicles, etc.
- **Specific bequests** (if any)
- **Residual estate**: Distribution to your children **equally** (or as specified)

> **Note:** Under [Article (5)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_3)), funeral expenses, administration costs, and debts must be settled **before** distribution.

### ### 5. **Conditions and Restrictions**
- Age at which children can inherit (e.g., 25 years)
- Conditions for inheritance (e.g., completion of education, marriage)
- Trust arrangements (if applicable)

### ### 6. **Revocation Clause**

### **1. DECLARATION OF TESTATOR**
I, **[Full Name of Testator]**, a **[Nationality]** national, born on **[Date of Birth]**, holding **[Emirates ID/Passport Number]**, residing in **[Full Address in UAE]**, being of sound mind and legal capacity, do hereby make, publish, and declare this to be my **Last Will and Testament**, hereby revoking all former wills and testamentary dispositions made by me.

> **Note:** This will must be registered with the **Dubai Courts’ Wills Service Centre (DIFC Wills & Probate Registry)** or the competent court in your emirate to be enforceable.

I hereby appoint **[Full Name of Executor]**, a **[Nationality]** national, born on **[Date of Birth]**, holding **[Emirates ID/Passport Number]**, residing at **[Full Address]**, as the **Executor** of this will.

  I appoint **[Full Name of Alternate Executor]**, a **[Nationality]** national, born on **[Date of Birth]**, holding **[Emirates ID/Passport Number]**, residing at **[Full Address]**, as the alternate Executor in the event the primary Executor is unable or unwilling to act.

> **Legal Requirement:** The Executor must not be convicted of a felony or crime affecting honour/trustworthiness unless rehabilitated ([Article (14)](Source:_Law_No._(15)_of_2017.pdf_(Page_7)).

### **4. DISTRIBUTION OF MY ESTATE**

#### **4.2 Cash and Other Assets**

## Report: Draft Will for AED 10,000,000 Estate with Two Children

---

### Overview
This report provides a **draft Will** for a **non-Muslim testator** with an **estate valued at AED 10,000,000** and **two children**, structured in accordance with **Federal Decree-Law No. (5) of 1985 (Civil Transactions Law of the UAE)** and **Law No. (15) of 2017 (DIFC Wills and Probate Registry Regulations)**. The draft is designed for registration under the **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry**, which is the primary mechanism for non-Muslims to register Wills in the UAE.

> **Pro-Tip:** Under UAE law, **non-Muslims** may register Wills with the **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry** to ensure their estate is distributed according to their wishes rather than under Sharia law. Muslim estates are governed by Sharia unless a valid non-Muslim Will is registered.

---

### Draft Will

---

#### **LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT**
**I, [Full Name of Testator], a non-Muslim of full legal capacity, holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address in UAE],**

**DO HEREBY MAKE, DECLARE, AND PUBLISH THIS MY LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT**, revoking all former Wills and testamentary dispositions, in the following terms:

---

### **ARTICLE 1: APPOINTMENT OF EXECUTOR**
1.1 I **hereby appoint** [Full Name of Executor], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address], as the **sole Executor** of this Will.

1.2 If the appointed Executor is unable or unwilling to act, I appoint [Full Name of Alternate Executor], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address], as the **alternate Executor**.

> **Legal Reference:** Article (14)(a)(4) of **Law No. (15) of 2017** requires an Executor to declare acceptance and meet eligibility criteria (full capacity, no felony convictions, not bankrupt unless rehabilitated, no interest in the willed property).

---

### **ARTICLE 2: APPOINTMENT OF GUARDIAN(S) FOR MINOR CHILDREN**
2.1 I **hereby appoint** [Full Name of Guardian 1], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address], and [Full Name of Guardian 2], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address], as **joint guardians** of my minor children: **[Child 1 Name, Date of Birth]** and **[Child 2 Name, Date of Birth]**.

2.2 In the event both guardians are unable or unwilling to act, I appoint **[Full Name of Alternate Guardian]**, holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Full Address], as the **alternate guardian**.

> **Legal Note:** UAE law does not explicitly govern guardianship in Wills but recognizes testamentary guardianship under **Article 1230 of the Civil Transactions Law**. The Family Guidance Committee or UAE courts will ultimately approve guardianship arrangements.

---
### **ARTICLE 3: SPECIFIC BEQUESTS**
3.1 I bequeath the following **specific assets** (if any) to the named beneficiaries:
- **AED [Amount] in cash** to **[Beneficiary Name]**, holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Address].
- **Real property located at [Address/Plot Number]** to **[Beneficiary Name]**, holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number].
- **Vehicle [Make, Model, Year, Plate Number]** to **[Beneficiary Name]**.

3.2 If any specific bequest cannot be fulfilled (e.g., asset sold or lost), the bequeathed amount shall lapse and form part of the residual estate.

---
### **ARTICLE 4: RESIDUAL ESTATE DISTRIBUTION**
4.1 All remaining assets of my estate, after payment of debts, funeral expenses, administration costs, and specific bequests, shall be distributed as follows:
- **[Child 1 Name]**: **50% (AED 5,000,000)**
- **[Child 2 Name]**: **50% (AED 5,000,000)**

> **Legal Reference:** Under **Article 5 of Law No. (15) of 2017**, a Will takes precedence over intestate succession. The residual estate is distributed per the testator’s wishes, subject to priority of debts and administration expenses.

---
### **ARTICLE 5: PAYMENT OF DEBTS AND FUNERAL EXPENSES**
5.1 My Executor shall, in the following order of priority, settle:
1. **Funeral expenses** of my burial/cremation and related ceremonies.
2. **Estate administration and Will implementation expenses** (e.g., legal fees, court costs, valuation fees).
3. **Remuneration of the Executor and any Administrator** (up to **2% of the gross estate value** as reasonable remuneration, unless otherwise agreed by the beneficiaries).
4. **Valid debts** owed by me at the time of my death (e.g., mortgages, loans, credit cards), provided such debts are evidenced in writing.

5.2 If the estate is insufficient to cover all liabilities, the Executor shall distribute available funds in the order above.

> **Legal Reference:** Article (5) of **Law No. (15) of 2017** mandates priority of funeral expenses, administration costs, and debts.

---
### **ARTICLE 6: POWERS OF THE EXECUTOR**
6.1 My Executor is granted the **following powers**, exercisable without court approval unless otherwise stated:
- To **collect, manage, and safeguard** all estate assets.
- To **sell, lease, or mortgage** estate assets to pay debts or administration costs, provided such actions are in the best interests of the beneficiaries.
- To **invest estate funds** in Sharia-compliant or conventional instruments, as deemed prudent.
- To **distribute the estate** to beneficiaries upon finalization of debts and administration.
- To **engage professionals** (lawyers, valuers, accountants) and pay their fees from the estate, provided such fees are reasonable and approved by the beneficiaries or the DIFC Courts.

> **Legal Reference:** Article (23) of **Law No. (15) of 2017** outlines the duties and powers of Executors/Administrators.

---
### **ARTICLE 7: CONDITIONS AND RESTRICTIONS**
7.1 This Will shall take effect **immediately upon my death**.

7.2 If any beneficiary **predeceases me**, their share shall lapse and be distributed equally among the surviving beneficiaries.

7.3 If any beneficiary is a minor at the time of distribution, their share shall be held in **trust** by the Executor until the beneficiary attains **21 years of age**, at which point the share shall be distributed.

7.4 No beneficiary shall have the right to **encumber, sell, or transfer** their interest in the estate prior to final distribution.

---
### **ARTICLE 8: GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION**
8.1 This Will shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the **United Arab Emirates**, specifically:
- **Federal Decree-Law No. (5) of 1985 (Civil Transactions Law)**
- **Law No. (15) of 2017 (DIFC Wills and Probate Registry Regulations)**

8.2 Any disputes arising from this Will shall be resolved through the **DIFC Courts** or the **UAE Civil Courts**, at the discretion of the Executor or beneficiaries.

---
### **ARTICLE 9: MISCELLANEOUS**
9.1 I **hereby revoke** all former Wills and testamentary dispositions made by me.

9.2 This Will is written in **English and Arabic** (if applicable), and both versions are equally authentic.

9.3 If any provision of this Will is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force.

---
### **ARTICLE 10: EXECUTION AND REGISTRATION**
10.1 I **hereby declare** that I am of **sound mind and full legal capacity** and sign this Will freely and without duress.

10.2 **Witnesses:**
- **Witness 1:** [Full Name], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Address]
- **Witness 2:** [Full Name], holding [Passport/Emirates ID Number], residing at [Address]

10.3 This Will shall be **registered with the DIFC Wills and Probate Registry** within **30 days** of execution to ensure enforceability under UAE law.

> **Legal Requirement:** **Article 8 of Law No. (15) of 2017** requires Wills to be registered by non-Muslims with the DIFC Wills and Probate Registry to be valid under UAE law.

---
### **ARTICLE 11: ENTIRE AGREEMENT**
This Will constitutes the **entire agreement** between me and my beneficiaries regarding the distribution of my estate.

---
### **SIGNATURES**
**Signed by the Testator:**
[Signature of Testator]
[Full Name of Testator]
[Date: DD/MM/YYYY]

**Signed by Witness 1:**
[Signature of Witness 1]
[Full Name of Witness 1]
[Date: DD/MM/YYYY]

**Signed by Witness 2:**
[Signature of Witness 2]
[Full Name of Witness 2]
[Date: DD/MM/YYYY]

---
### **IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS FOR THE TESTATOR**
- **Tax Implications:** The UAE does not impose **inheritance tax** or **estate duty**. However, beneficiaries may be subject to **income tax** in their country of residence on inherited income.
- **Currency:** All monetary amounts are in **AED (United Arab Emirates Dirham)**.
- **Assets Abroad:** If the testator owns assets outside the UAE, a **separate Will** should be drafted for each jurisdiction or a **multi-jurisdictional Will** should be considered.
- **Sharia vs. Will:** Without a registered non-Muslim Will, Sharia law would apply to the estate distribution, potentially differing from the testator’s wishes.
- **Updating the Will:** The testator should review and update the Will every **2–3 years** or upon major life events (e.g., birth of a child, marriage, divorce, acquisition of new assets).

---
### **NEXT STEPS**
1. **Consult a UAE-based estate planning lawyer** to finalize the Will and ensure compliance with **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry requirements**.
2. **Register the Will** with the **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry** ([www.difcwillregistry.ae](https://www.difcwillregistry.ae)).
3. **Inform the Executor and Guardians** of their roles and provide them with a copy of the Will.
4. **Store the original Will** in a secure location (e.g., DIFC Wills Registry safe deposit box or with the testator’s lawyer).
5. **Review the Will** periodically or after major life events.

---
### **DISCLAIMER**
> This draft is provided for **informational purposes only** and does not constitute **legal, tax, or financial advice**. The testator should obtain **professional legal counsel** in the UAE to ensure the Will complies with all applicable laws and accurately reflects their intentions. The DIFC Wills and Probate Registry or a UAE notary public must approve the final version of the Will.

## Wills and Estate Planning in the UAE: Key Considerations for Non-Muslims

### Legal Framework Governing Wills in the UAE
In the UAE, **wills** for non-Muslims are primarily governed by:
- **Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2021 on the Personal Status Law for Non-Muslims** (effective 1 February 2023), which applies to non-Muslim expatriates in the UAE.
- **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry** rules (for assets within the DIFC jurisdiction).
- **Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Wills Service** (for assets within the ADGM jurisdiction).

> **Pro-Tip:** If you are a non-Muslim resident in the UAE, you can opt to register your will under the **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry** or **ADGM Wills Service**, which allows you to distribute your estate according to your wishes (e.g., to your children and wife), rather than under **Sharia-based inheritance rules** that would otherwise apply by default under UAE civil law.

---

### Types of Wills Available in the UAE

#### 1. **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry Will**
- Applies to assets located in or connected to the **DIFC** (e.g., property, bank accounts, investments registered in DIFC).
- Allows you to specify **beneficiaries**, including your **wife** and **two children**, and how your estate is divided.
- Must be drafted in English or Arabic, signed in the presence of two witnesses, and registered with the **DIFC Wills Service**.
- Valid for **lifetime** and can be updated or revoked.

#### 2. **ADGM Wills Service Will**
- Similar to DIFC Wills but applicable to assets in or connected to the **ADGM**.
- Also allows for **custom distribution** of assets.

#### 3. **UAE Local Will (Non-Muslim Will)**
- Some Emirates (e.g., Dubai, Sharjah) allow non-Muslims to register wills with local authorities (e.g., **Dubai Courts**, **Sharjah Courts**) under non-Muslim inheritance rules.
- These wills are typically drafted in Arabic and follow local procedures.

> **Important:** Without a registered will, your estate may be distributed under **Sharia inheritance rules** by default, which may not align with your wishes (e.g., daughters may not inherit equal shares to sons under Sharia).

---

### Key Considerations for Your Estate (10 Million AED + Properties)

#### 1. **Asset Distribution**
- Under **Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2021**, you can specify:
  - Your **wife** as a beneficiary (e.g., a fixed share or lifetime usufruct over the marital home).
  - Your **two children** as equal or unequal beneficiaries (e.g., 50% each).
  - You can also include **guardianship provisions** for minor children.
- Example distribution:
  - **Wife**: 30% of the estate (or specific assets, e.g., the marital home).
  - **Child 1**: 35% of the estate.
  - **Child 2**: 35% of the estate.

#### 2. **Executor and Trustee**
- Appoint an **executor** (e.g., a trusted family member, friend, or professional) to administer your estate.
- Consider appointing a **guardian** for minor children if applicable.

#### 3. **Guardianship for Minor Children**
- If your children are minors, specify who will act as their **legal guardian** and **financial trustee** until they reach adulthood (age 21 in the UAE).

#### 4. **Real Estate Specifics**
- For **apartment buildings and other properties**, ensure the will clearly identifies:
  - The **property details** (address, title deed number, land department reference).
  - The **percentage share** each beneficiary receives.
- If properties are mortgaged or encumbered, disclose this in the will.

#### 5. **Digital Assets and Bank Accounts**
- Include provisions for **bank accounts**, **investments**, **digital assets**, and **business interests** to avoid disputes.

---
### Registration and Validity Requirements

#### 1. **DIFC Wills Registration**
- **Eligibility**: Non-Muslims with assets in the UAE (including Dubai, Abu Dhabi, etc.).
- **Process**:
  1. Draft the will in English or Arabic.
  2. Sign in the presence of **two witnesses** (not beneficiaries).
  3. Attest the will at a **notary public** in DIFC.
  4. Register with the **DIFC Wills and Probate Registry**.
- **Cost**: ~AED 10,000–15,000 (varies by complexity).
- **Validity**: Recognized across the UAE and internationally.

#### 2. **ADGM Wills Registration**
- Similar process to DIFC but under ADGM jurisdiction.
- Cost: ~AED 8,000–12,000.

#### 3. **Local UAE Wills (e.g., Dubai Courts)**
- Draft in Arabic, notarize, and register with local courts.
- Cost: Lower than DIFC/ADGM but less flexible for non-Muslims.

> **Pro-Tip:** Register your will **before** any health issues arise. DIFC/ADGM wills are **not valid** if signed under duress or when the testator lacks mental capacity.

---
### Inheritance Rules Without a Will (Default Sharia Rules)
If you **do not** register a will:
- Your estate may be distributed under **Sharia inheritance rules**, which typically allocate:
  - **Wife**: 1/8 of the estate (if children exist).
  - **Children**: Remaining 7/8, with **sons receiving twice the share of daughters** (e.g., if two sons and two daughters, sons get 2/3, daughters get 1/3).
- **Real estate** may be subject to **forced heirship rules**, limiting your ability to distribute properties freely.

---
### Practical Steps to Draft Your Will

1. **Consult a Specialist Lawyer**:
   - Engage a **UAE-based wills and estate planning lawyer** (e.g., in DIFC, ADGM, or local courts).
   - Ensure the lawyer is registered with the **DIFC Wills Service** or **ADGM Wills Registry**.

2. **Gather Documentation**:
   - Title deeds for all properties.
   - Bank account statements and investment details.
   - Passports and Emirates IDs of beneficiaries.
   - Details of any mortgages or loans on properties.

3. **Draft the Will**:
   - Specify **beneficiaries** (wife, children) and **asset distribution**.
   - Include **executor**, **guardian**, and **trustee** provisions.
   - Address **debts and taxes** (e.g., UAE has no inheritance tax, but estate administration may incur fees).

4. **Register the Will**:
   - Choose **DIFC** or **ADGM** for maximum flexibility.
   - Complete registration and obtain a **certificate of validity**.

5. **Review and Update**:
   - Review the will every **2–3 years** or after major life events (e.g., birth of a child, divorce, purchase of new property).

---
### Costs and Timeline

| Item | Estimated Cost (AED) | Timeline |
|---|---|---|
| DIFC Will Registration | 10,000–15,000 | 2–4 weeks |
| ADGM Will Registration | 8,000–12,000 | 2–4 weeks |
| Local UAE Will (e.g., Dubai Courts) | 3,000–8,000 | 1–2 weeks |
| Notary and Translation Fees | 1,000–3,000 | 1 week |

---
### Common Mistakes to Avoid

- **Not registering the will**: An unregistered will may not be enforceable under non-Muslim rules.
- **Vague descriptions**: Avoid ambiguous language (e.g., "my properties" without details).
- **Ignoring debts**: Ensure the will accounts for mortgages or loans on properties.
- **Outdated wills**: Failing to update after major life changes (e.g., marriage, birth of a child).

---
### Next Steps

1. **Contact a UAE wills specialist lawyer** (e.g., in DIFC or ADGM) to draft and register your will.
2. **Provide full asset details** (properties, bank accounts, investments).
3. **Specify your beneficiaries** (wife, children) and distribution percentages.
4. **Appoint an executor and guardian** (if applicable).
5. **Register the will** and store the original safely (e.g., with the DIFC Wills Registry).

> **Warning:** Do **not** use generic online will templates. UAE laws require **local registration** and **notarization** for validity. Always work with a licensed UAE lawyer.

## Qualifying Income – UAE Corporate Tax Treatment

| **Type of Qualifying Income** | **Tax Treatment** | **Relevant Article** |
|---|---|---|

| Dividends and capital gains from foreign shareholdings (subject to conditions) | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(b) |
| Income from operating aircraft or ships in international traffic (non-resident) | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(c) |
| Income from disposal of shares/securities in a UAE company (non-resident) | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(d) |
| Income of foreign permanent establishments of a UAE resident (subject to conditions) | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(e) |
| Income of UAE government and government-controlled entities | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(f) |
| Income of extractive and non-extractive natural resource businesses (subject to conditions) | **0%** Corporate Tax on exempt income | Art. 4(1)(g) |
| **Qualifying income** of a **Qualifying Free Zone Person** (meeting substance, transaction, and audit requirements) | **0%** Corporate Tax on qualifying income | Art. 19(1) |
| Taxable income of a **Small Business Relief** claimant (revenue ≤ AED 3,000,000 for tax periods ending before 31 Dec 2026) | **0%** Corporate Tax on taxable income up to AED 375,000; **9%** above that threshold | Art. 21 |
| Taxable income exceeding AED 375,000 (where no exemption or relief applies) | **9%** Corporate Tax on taxable income above AED 375,000 | Art. 3(1) |

## Qualifying Income and Tax Treatment under UAE Corporate Tax

> **Pro-Tip:** **Qualifying income** refers to income that meets specific criteria set out in the Corporate Tax regime and may be eligible for exemption or preferential treatment.

| **Type of Income** | **Description** | **Tax Treatment** | **Relevant Article** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings** | Dividends and capital gains earned by a UAE resident company from ownership interests of at least **5%** held for at least **12 months** | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(a) |
| **Dividends and capital gains for pension/social security/investment funds** | Dividends and capital gains earned by a UAE resident pension or social security fund, or a UAE resident investment fund from its ownership interests | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(b) |
| **International transportation income** | Income earned by a non-resident person from operating aircraft or ships in international transportation (subject to reciprocal treatment) | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(c) |
| **Investment returns of non-residents** | Income earned by a non-resident person from dividends, interest, capital gains, royalties and other investment returns, and from the disposal of shares or securities in a UAE resident company (provided no PE in UAE) | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(d) |
| **Disposal of shares/securities by non-residents** | Income earned by a non-resident person from the disposal of shares or securities in a non-resident company (provided no PE in UAE and the value does not derive from immovable property in UAE) | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(e) |
| **Other prescribed income** | Income as may be prescribed by the Cabinet | **Exempt** from Corporate Tax | Article 4(1)(f) |
| **Taxable income ≤ AED 375,000** | Taxable income of a taxable person that does not exceed **AED 375,000** | **0%** Corporate Tax rate | Article 3(1) |
| **Taxable income > AED 375,000** | Taxable income exceeding **AED 375,000** | **9%** Corporate Tax rate | Article 3(1) |
| **Small Business Relief** | Taxable persons with revenue ≤ **AED 3 million** for tax periods ending before **31 December 2026** | **0%** Corporate Tax rate (elective) | Article 21 |
| **Qualifying Free Zone Person** | A **Free Zone Person** that meets the conditions under Article 3 | **0%** Corporate Tax rate on **qualifying income**; **9%** on other income | Article 3 |
| **Transfer Pricing adjustments** | Transactions between related parties or connected persons must comply with the **arm’s length principle** | Adjustments may increase taxable income if not at arm’s length | Article 34 |
tell me about qualifing income

## Qualifying Income under UAE Corporate Tax

### Definition and Scope
**Qualifying income** refers to income that meets specific criteria under **Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022** to be treated as exempt from UAE Corporate Tax or subject to a **0% tax rate**, depending on the category.

### Categories of Qualifying Income

#### 1. Exempt Income (Article 4)
Income that is specifically **exempt** from UAE Corporate Tax includes:

- **Dividends and capital gains** from **qualifying shareholdings** (minimum **5% ownership** for at least **12 months**)
- **Dividends and capital gains** from foreign subsidiaries (subject to conditions)
- **Income from operating aircraft or ships in international traffic** by non-residents
- **Income of foreign governments, international organizations**, and other exempt persons
- **Income from immovable property** located in the UAE if subject to Real Estate Tax
- **Income from UAE government entities** or government-controlled entities

#### 2. Qualifying Activities Income for Free Zone Persons (Article 18)
Income derived from **qualifying activities** by a **qualifying free zone person** may be subject to a **0% Corporate Tax rate**, provided all conditions are met:

- **Qualifying activities** include:
  - Manufacturing and processing
  - Holding company activities
  - Fund management
  - Treasury and financing
  - Financing and leasing of aircraft
  - Distribution in or from a designated zone
  - Trading of qualifying commodities
  - Regulated financial services
  - Headquarters services to related parties
  - Treasury and financing services to related parties
  - Investment management
  - Ancillary activities

- **Conditions** include:
  - Maintaining adequate substance in the UAE
  - Not conducting business with mainland UAE (subject to exceptions)
  - Complying with **transfer pricing rules** (Article 34)
  - Meeting substance requirements

#### 3. Other Qualifying Income Categories
- **Income from UAE government-issued debt instruments** (may be exempt)
- **Income from foreign-sourced dividends** (may be exempt if certain conditions are met)
- **Capital gains** from disposal of assets that generate exempt income

### Key Requirements
- Must comply with **arm’s length principle** for transactions with related parties under **Transfer Pricing rules** (Article 34)
- Must maintain proper documentation and records
- Must comply with **substance requirements** for free zone persons
- Must not engage in **mainland UAE business activities** (except as permitted)

### Tax Treatment
| Income Type | Tax Rate | Legal Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Exempt income | **0%** | Article 4 |
| Qualifying activities income (Free Zone) | **0%** (subject to conditions) | Article 18 |
| Taxable income up to **AED 375,000** | **0%** | Article 3 |
| Taxable income above **AED 375,000** | **9%** | Article 3 |

### Important Notes
- **Small Business Relief** (Article 21) applies to businesses with revenue ≤ **AED 3,000,000** for tax periods ending before **31 December 2026**
- **Transfer Pricing documentation** must be maintained for transactions with related parties (Article 34)
- **Exempt persons** must be registered with the **Federal Tax Authority**

messages.content: Explain e-invoicing in UAE and Peppol requirements briefly

## E-Invoicing in the UAE and Peppol Requirements

E-invoicing in the UAE refers to the **mandatory electronic issuance and storage of tax invoices and credit/debit notes** in a standardized format, as required by the **Federal Tax Authority (FTA)** under the **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on VAT** and its executive regulations.

---

### ## E-Invoicing Mandate in the UAE

The UAE e-invoicing mandate is being implemented in **two phases**, as per the **FTA e-invoicing regulations**:

| Phase | Applicability | Effective Date |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| **Phase 1** | **Large taxpayers** (as defined by FTA) | **1 July 2025** |
| **Phase 2** | All other **VAT-registered businesses** | **1 January 2026** |

> **Pro-Tip:** The FTA will notify taxpayers of their phase assignment via the FTA e-Services portal. Taxpayers must comply with the **Peppol e-invoicing standard** once their phase begins.

---

### ## Peppol Requirements in the UAE

The UAE has adopted the **Pan-European Public Procurement Online (Peppol) framework** for e-invoicing, as mandated by the **UAE Peppol Authority** (operated under the FTA).

#### ### 1. Peppol ID Registration

A **Peppol ID** is a unique identifier required for all VAT-registered businesses subject to e-invoicing. It is used to **exchange e-invoices** via the Peppol network.

- **Peppol ID Registration Threshold**:
  - Mandatory for businesses with **annual taxable turnover ≥ AED 375,000** (as per **Article 61 of the VAT Law** and **Cabinet Decision No. (4) of 2023**).
  - Voluntary for businesses below the threshold but encouraged to adopt e-invoicing early.

- **Peppol ID Format**:
  - Follows the **ISO/IEC 15459-1** standard.
  - Example: `008801234567890` (UAE TRN-based format).

#### ### 2. Peppol Registration Process

To register for a **Peppol ID** and access the Peppol network:

1. **Ensure VAT Registration**:
   - Hold a valid **Tax Registration Number (TRN)** issued by the FTA.

2. **Select a Peppol Access Point Provider**:
   - Choose an FTA-approved **Peppol Access Point provider** (e.g., local or international providers accredited by the **OpenPeppol AISBL**).

3. **Submit Registration via FTA e-Services**:
   - Log in to the **FTA e-Services portal**.
   - Navigate to **Peppol Registration**.
   - Provide:
     - Valid **TRN**
     - Business details (name, address)
     - **Peppol Access Point provider** details
   - Submit and receive confirmation (typically within **5-10 business days**).

> **Pro-Tip:** The FTA provides a list of approved **Peppol Access Point providers** on its official website. Ensure your provider supports the **Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 profile**.

#### ### 3. Technical Specifications for E-Invoices

All e-invoices must comply with the **Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 profile**, which is based on:

- **UBL 2.1** (Universal Business Language) standard.
- **Peppol BIS Billing 3.0** specifications (aligned with **EN 16931** EU standard).

Key technical requirements:
- **XML format** (UBL 2.1).
- **Digital signature** (qualified or advanced) for authenticity and integrity.
- **QR code** on invoices for easy verification.
- **Peppol ID** must be included in the invoice metadata for cross-border transactions.

---
### ## UAE VAT Rates and E-Invoicing Implications

E-invoices must reflect the correct **VAT treatment** based on the **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on VAT**:

| VAT Rate | Applicability | Example Use Cases |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| **5% (Standard)** | General taxable supplies | Most goods and services |
| **0% (Zero-Rated)** | Exports, international transport, certain healthcare/education | Exports outside GCC, international passenger transport |
| **Exempt** | Residential property, bare land, local passenger transport, financial services | Renting residential property, local bus services |

> **Note:** The **place of supply** rules (Article 26 of the VAT Law) determine whether a supply is subject to UAE VAT. For cross-border transactions, the **Peppol ID** must be referenced to ensure compliance.

---
### ## Filing VAT Returns (FTA VAT-201)

While not part of e-invoicing itself, VAT returns must be filed electronically via the FTA portal:

- **Form**: **VAT-201** (VAT Return).
- **Frequency**:
  - **Quarterly** (for most taxpayers).
  - **Monthly** (for high-volume taxpayers, as notified by FTA).
- **Deadline**: **28th day** of the month following the end of the tax period.
- **Submission**: Via the **FTA e-Services portal**.

> **Pro-Tip:** Ensure all e-invoices are **archived for at least 5 years** (as per FTA record-keeping requirements).

---
### ## Summary of Key Steps

1. **Check VAT registration threshold** (AED 375,000).
2. **Register for Peppol ID** via FTA e-Services (if applicable).
3. **Select a Peppol Access Point provider**.
4. **Generate UBL 2.1 e-invoices** compliant with Peppol BIS Billing 3.0.
5. **Issue e-invoices** via the Peppol network.
6. **File VAT returns (VAT-201)** by the 28th day deadline.
explain me e-invoicing, and how I can implement in my Tally ERP  right now

## E-Invoicing in the UAE: What It Is and How to Implement It in Tally ERP

---

### ## What is E-Invoicing in the UAE?

E-Invoicing in the UAE is a **mandatory digital invoicing system** introduced by the **Federal Tax Authority (FTA)** to standardize invoice issuance, transmission, and storage for VAT-registered businesses. It replaces paper and PDF invoices with **structured, machine-readable electronic invoices** that are transmitted via the **Peppol network** (Pan-European Public Procoy Procurement Online).

> **Key Legal Basis**:
> - **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on VAT** (Articles 26, 55, and 68) mandates digital record-keeping and invoice issuance.
> - **FTA E-Invoicing Decision** (Cabinet Decision No. 46 of 2021) and **FTA E-Invoicing Technical Specifications** require compliance with Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 (UBL 2.1 format).
> - **Peppol Authority UAE** oversees Peppol ID registration and network compliance.

#### ### E-Invoicing Phases in the UAE
| Phase | Applicability | Deadline | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | Large taxpayers (VAT turnover ≥ **AED 375 million**) | 1 October 2021 | Mandatory e-invoicing issuance and receipt via Peppol |
| **Phase 2** | All remaining VAT-registered businesses | 1 April 2022 | Mandatory e-invoicing issuance and receipt via Peppol |

> **Pro-Tip**:
> Even if your turnover is below the **AED 375,000** VAT registration threshold, once you **voluntarily register for VAT**, you must comply with e-invoicing rules if your taxable turnover exceeds **AED 187,500** (50% of the mandatory threshold) — as per **FTA guidance on voluntary registration**.

---

### ## Why Use E-Invoicing?

- **Compliance**: Meets FTA legal requirements.
- **Fraud Prevention**: Reduces fake invoices and tax evasion.
- **Automation**: Enables faster processing, reconciliation, and VAT return filing.
- **Global Standard**: Uses **Peppol**, the international e-invoicing standard, supporting cross-border trade.

---

### ## How to Implement E-Invoicing in Tally ERP (Step-by-Step)

To implement e-invoicing in **Tally ERP 9 or TallyPrime**, follow these steps:

---

#### ### Step 1: Ensure You Are VAT-Registered and Have a Valid TRN

- You must have a **Tax Registration Number (TRN)** issued by the FTA.
- Log in to the **FTA portal** ([https://eservices.tax.gov.ae](https://eservices.tax.gov.ae)) to confirm your TRN status.

> **Note**: If you are not VAT-registered, you **cannot issue tax invoices** and thus **cannot comply with e-invoicing**. You must register if your taxable turnover exceeds **AED 375,000** (mandatory) or voluntarily if above **AED 187,500**.

---

#### ### Step 2: Register for a Peppol ID (If Not Already Done)

A **Peppol ID** is required to send and receive e-invoices via the Peppol network.

- **Peppol ID Format**: `urn:peppol:entity:iso6523-actorid-upin:<TRN>`
  Example: `urn:peppol:entity:iso6523-actorid-upin:123456789000001`

- **How to Register**:
  1. Go to the **FTA e-Services portal** ([https://eservices.tax.gov.ae](https://eservices.tax.gov.ae)).
  2. Navigate to **Peppol Registration**.
  3. Enter your **TRN** and **Peppol Access Point provider** details.
  4. Submit and receive your **Peppol ID** within 2–3 business days.

> **Pro-Tip**:
> You must select a **Peppol Access Point Provider** approved by the **UAE Peppol Authority**. Popular providers include **ClearTax, Spectra, Mark IT Solutions**, and **Nandini Infosys** (see sources [2], [3], [4], [5]).

---

#### ### Step 3: Configure Tally ERP for E-Invoicing

##### #### 3.1: Update Tally to the Latest Version
- Ensure you are using **TallyPrime Release 3.0 or later**, or **Tally ERP 9 Release 6.6 or later**.
- Download updates from [Tally Solutions](https://www.tallysolutions.com).

##### #### 3.2: Enable E-Invoicing in Tally
1. Open **Tally ERP** or **TallyPrime**.
2. Go to:
   - **Gateway of Tally** → **F11: Features** → **F4: Statutory & Taxation**
3. Enable:
   - **Enable Goods and Services Tax (GST)** → **Yes**
   - **Enable E-Invoicing** → **Yes**
4. Enter your:
   - **TRN**
   - **Company Name** (as registered with FTA)
   - **Peppol ID** (from Step 2)
   - **Peppol Access Point Provider** (e.g., ClearTax, Spectra, etc.)

> **Source**: [Source 1: One-Time Setup for e-Invoicing in TallyPrime](https://help.tallysolutions.com/one-time-setup-for-e-invoicing/)

##### #### 3.3: Configure Invoice Format and QR Code
- Go to **F11 → F4 → E-Invoicing**
- Set:
  - **Invoice Type**: **Tax Invoice** (for standard-rated supplies)
  - **QR Code**: Enable **QR Code generation** (required for all invoices)
  - **E-Invoice Language**: English (default)
  - **E-Invoice Schema**: **UBL 2.1** (mandatory per FTA)

> **Pro-Tip**:
> Tally automatically generates a **QR code** containing:
> - Seller’s TRN
> - Invoice number
> - Invoice date
> - Total amount
> - VAT amount
> This QR code must appear on all printed invoices.

##### #### 3.4: Map VAT Rates and HS Codes
- Ensure all **VAT rates** are correctly mapped:
  - **5%**: Standard-rated supplies
  - **0%**: Zero-rated (exports, international transport, etc.)
  - **Exempt**: Residential rent, local passenger transport, etc.
- Assign **HS Codes** to goods/services in stock items for accurate classification.

> **Source**: [Source 3: E-Invoicing in Tally – Everything You Need To Know](https://www.markitsolutions.in/blog-details/e-invoicing-in-tally-everything-you-need-to-know)

---
#### ### Step 4: Generate and Validate an E-Invoice

##### #### 4.1: Create a Sales Invoice
1. Go to **Accounting Vouchers** → **F8: Sales**
2. Fill in:
   - Party details (with TRN)
   - Items with correct VAT rates
   - Payment terms
3. Press **Ctrl+E** (or click **E-Invoice**) to generate the e-invoice.

##### #### 4.2: Validate the E-Invoice
- Tally will:
  - Generate the **UBL 2.1 XML file**
  - Send it to your **Peppol Access Point Provider**
  - Receive an **IRN (Invoice Reference Number)** from the FTA system
  - Display the IRN on the invoice
- You can print or save the invoice with the **QR code and IRN**.

> **Pro-Tip**:
> The **IRN** is a unique 30-digit alphanumeric number issued by the FTA. It must be printed on the invoice and stored for 5 years.

> **Source**: [Source 4: Generate e-Invoice Instantly in TallyPrime](https://nandiniinfosys.com/everything-you-need-to-know-about-e-invoicing-and-how-to-implement-it-on-tallyprime/)

---
#### ### Step 5: Integrate with Peppol Access Point (Optional but Recommended)

If you want **automated transmission**, integrate Tally with a **Peppol Access Point Provider** like:
- **ClearTax** ([https://cleartax.in](https://cleartax.in)) – Source [2]
- **Spectra** ([https://spectracompunet.com](https://spectracompunet.com)) – Source [5]
- **Mark IT Solutions** ([https://www.markitsolutions.in](https://www.markitsolutions.in)) – Source [3]
- **Nandini Infosys** ([https://nandiniinfosys.com](https://nandiniinfosys.com)) – Source [4]

These providers offer:
- **Automated e-invoice generation and transmission**
- **Real-time IRN fetching**
- **Dashboard for invoice tracking**
- **Reconciliation and reporting**

> **Pro-Tip**:
> Using a **Tally Connector** (like ClearTax) allows you to:
> - Auto-push invoices to Peppol
> - Avoid manual steps
> - Get real-time validation and error alerts

---
### ## What Happens After Implementation?

- All **sales invoices** are automatically converted to **UBL 2.1 XML** and sent via Peppol.
- You receive **IRN** and can print invoices with **QR code and IRN**.
- Invoices are **stored digitally** for 5 years (FTA requirement).
- You can file **VAT-201 returns** using the same data (Tally can export VAT reports).

> **Reminder**:
> - File **VAT-201 return** by the **28th day** after the tax period ends.
> - Keep digital records of all e-invoices.

---
### ## Quick Checklist: Are You Ready?

| Task | Done? |
|---|---|
| VAT-registered with valid TRN | ☐ |
| Peppol ID registered via FTA portal | ☐ |
| Peppol Access Point Provider selected | ☐ |
| Tally ERP updated to latest version | ☐ |
| E-Invoicing enabled in Tally (F11 → F4) | ☐ |
| TRN, Peppol ID, and Access Point configured in Tally | ☐ |
| VAT rates and HS codes mapped | ☐ |
| Test invoice generated and validated | ☐ |

---
### ## Need Help?

- **Tally Help Center**: [https://help.tallysolutions.com](https://help.tallysolutions.com)
- **FTA E-Invoicing Portal**: [https://eservices.tax.gov.ae](https://eservices.tax.gov.ae)
- **Peppol Authority UAE**: [https://peppol.tax.gov.ae](https://peppol.tax.gov.ae)

> **Final Note**:
> E-Invoicing is **not optional** for VAT-registered businesses in the UAE. Implementing it in Tally ERP is straightforward once you have your **TRN, Peppol ID, and Access Point**. Start with the **one-time setup**, test with a sample invoice, and go live.

## The Peppol Network: A Deep Dive into Its Architecture, Components, and Operation

---

### ## What Is the Peppol Network?

The **Peppol network** (Pan-European Public Procurement Online) is a **global, open, standards-based e-procurement and e-invoicing network**. It enables secure, interoperable exchange of electronic documents—such as **invoices, purchase orders, and credit notes**—between businesses and government entities across borders and sectors.

> **Note**: Despite its name, Peppol is **not limited to Europe**. It is now used worldwide, including in the **UAE**, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, and Canada, under the governance of **OpenPeppol AISBL**, a non-profit international association based in Belgium.

---

### ## Core Purpose of Peppol

Peppol was designed to:
- Eliminate paper-based and PDF invoicing.
- Reduce manual data entry and errors.
- Enable **real-time, automated invoice processing**.
- Support **cross-border trade** with standardized formats.
- Ensure **legal compliance** with tax and procurement regulations.

> **Source**: [Source 2: What is Peppol? Complete Guide to the Peppol Network](https://poppel.app/guide/peppol-explained)

---

### ## How the Peppol Network Works: The Four-Corner Model

Peppol operates on a **four-corner model**, which defines how senders and receivers connect securely and reliably.

| Corner | Role | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Corner 1** | **Sender’s Access Point** | Your ERP (e.g., Tally ERP) or accounting software |
| **Corner 2** | **Sender’s Peppol Access Point Provider** | ClearTax, Spectra, Mark IT Solutions |
| **Corner 3** | **Receiver’s Peppol Access Point Provider** | Same or different provider as sender |
| **Corner 4** | **Receiver’s ERP or Accounting System** | Your customer’s ERP |

- The sender’s system sends an invoice to its **Access Point Provider (Corner 2)**.
- The provider routes the invoice through the **Peppol network** to the recipient’s Access Point Provider (Corner 3).
- The recipient’s provider delivers the invoice to their system (Corner 4).
- No direct connection is needed between sender and receiver.

> **Pro-Tip**: > This model ensures **scalability, security, and interoperability**—even if sender and receiver use different software or providers.

> **Source**: [Source 3: What is Peppol: The Complete Guide to Peppol | TrueCommerce](https://www.truecommerce.com/blog/what-is-peppol/)

---

### ## Key Components of the Peppol Network

#### ### 1. **Peppol ID (Participant Identifier)**

A **Peppol ID** uniquely identifies a business or government entity on the network.

- **Format**: `urn:peppol:<scheme>:<identifier>`
- **Common Scheme**: `iso6523-actorid-upin` (used in UAE)
- **Example (UAE)**: `urn:peppol:entity:iso6523-actorid-upin:123456789000001`

> **Note**: In the UAE, the identifier is typically your **FTA Tax Registration Number (TRN)**.

#### ### 2. **Peppol Access Points**

- **Access Points** are **certified service providers** that connect businesses to the Peppol network.
- They:
  - Convert business documents (e.g., invoices) into **Peppol-compliant formats** (UBL 2.1).
  - Transmit documents securely over the network.
  - Handle routing, validation, and delivery.
- You **must register with an approved Access Point** to send or receive e-invoices.

> **Approved UAE Access Points** include:
> - ClearTax ([https://cleartax.ae](https://cleartax.ae))
> - Spectra ([https://spectracompunet.com](https://spectracompunet.com))
> - Mark IT Solutions ([https://www.markitsolutions.in](https://www.markitsolutions.in))
> - Nandini Infosys ([https://nandiniinfosys.com](https://nandiniinfosys.com))

> **Source**: [Source 2](https://poppel.app/guide/peppol-explained), [Source 5](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/peppol-e-invoicing-network-compliance-guide)

#### ### 3. **Service Metadata Locator (SML)**

- Acts as the **global phonebook** of the Peppol network.
- Stores the **network address (URL)** of each **Service Metadata Publisher (SMP)**.
- When you send an invoice, your Access Point queries the **SML** to find the recipient’s SMP.

#### ### 4. **Service Metadata Publisher (SMP)**

- Hosts the **technical configuration** for a participant (e.g., supported document types, endpoints).
- Your Access Point uses the **SMP** to:
  - Validate the recipient’s Peppol ID.
  - Determine how to deliver the document.
  - Ensure compatibility with the recipient’s system.

> **Source**: [Source 4: Receiving Electronic Invoices Through the Peppol Network in SAP S/4HANA](https://community.sap.com/t5/financial-management-blog-posts-by-sap/receiving-electronic-invoices-through-the-peppol-network-in-sap-s-4hana-or/ba-p/13968706)

---

### ## Document Standards and Message Types

Peppol uses **standardized document formats** to ensure interoperability.

| Document Type | Peppol Standard | Format | Use Case |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Invoice** | Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 | UBL 2.1 XML | Tax invoices, credit notes |
| **Order** | Peppol BIS Ordering 3.0 | UBL 2.1 XML | Purchase orders |
| **Catalogue** | Peppol BIS Catalogue 3.0 | UBL 2.1 XML | Product catalogues |

> **Key Point**: > The **UAE FTA mandates UBL 2.1** for e-invoicing, aligned with **Peppol BIS Billing 3.0**.

> **Source**: [Source 1: Peppol Explained: Understanding How It Works and Its Role](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/peppol-network-oriol-baus%C3%A0-xi2zf)

---

### ## How a Document Travels Through the Peppol Network (Step-by-Step)

1. **Sender creates invoice** in ERP (e.g., Tally ERP).
2. **Sender’s Access Point** (e.g., ClearTax) receives the invoice.
3. **Access Point validates** the invoice format and recipient’s Peppol ID.
4. **Access Point queries SML** to find the recipient’s **SMP**.
5. **Access Point sends invoice to recipient’s Access Point** via the Peppol network.
6. **Recipient’s Access Point** delivers the invoice to their ERP.
7. **Recipient’s system** processes the invoice automatically.

> **Visual Flow**:
> ```
> Tally ERP → ClearTax (Sender AP) → Peppol Network → Spectra (Receiver AP) → Customer ERP
> ```

> **Source**: [Source 3](https://www.truecommerce.com/blog/what-is-peppol/), [Source 4](https://community.sap.com/t5/financial-management-blog-posts-by-sap/receiving-electronic-invoices-through-the-peppol-network-in-sap-s-4hana-or/ba-p/13968706)

---

### ## Governance and Standardization

- **OpenPeppol AISBL** (Belgium) is the **global governance body**.
  - Sets technical standards.
  - Certifies Access Points.
  - Manages the SML and SMP infrastructure.
- **National Peppol Authorities** (e.g., **Peppol Authority UAE**) oversee local compliance and registration.
  - In the UAE, the **FTA** acts as the Peppol Authority.

> **Source**: [Source 2](https://poppel.app/guide/peppol-explained), [Source 5](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/peppol-e-invoicing-network-compliance-guide)

---

### ## Peppol in the UAE: Regulatory Context

- The **UAE FTA** adopted Peppol as the **mandatory e-invoicing standard** under:
  - **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on VAT** (Articles 26, 55, 68).
  - **Cabinet Decision No. 46 of 2021** on e-invoicing.
  - **FTA E-Invoicing Technical Specifications** (UBL 2.1, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0).

- **Registration**:
  - Businesses register for a **Peppol ID** via the **FTA e-Services portal**.
  - Requires a valid **TRN**.

- **Mandate**:
  - **Phase 1**: Large taxpayers (turnover ≥ AED 375M) – from 1 Oct 2021.
  - **Phase 2**: All VAT-registered businesses – from 1 Apr 2022.

> **Pro-Tip**: > Even if your turnover is below AED 375,000, **voluntary VAT registration** triggers e-invoicing obligations if you issue taxable invoices.

> **Source**: [Source 2](https://poppel.app/guide/peppol-explained), [Source 5](https://www.getsphere.com/blog/peppol-e-invoicing-network-compliance-guide)

---
### ## Security and Compliance Features

- **End-to-end encryption** ensures document confidentiality.
- **Digital signatures** are not required but **QR codes** are mandatory in the UAE for invoice validation.
- **Audit trails** are maintained for 5 years (FTA requirement).
- **No central database** of invoices—documents are transmitted peer-to-peer.

---
### ## Why Businesses Prefer Peppol

| Benefit | Explanation |
|---|---|
| **Global Reach** | Connect with suppliers/customers worldwide using one network |
| **Interoperability** | Works across ERPs, accounting software, and government portals |
| **Automation** | Reduces manual data entry and errors |
| **Compliance** | Meets local and international tax and procurement rules |
| **Scalability** | Supports high-volume invoice exchange |

---
### ## Common Misconceptions

| Misconception | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Peppol is only for Europe." | Peppol is **global** and used in UAE, Singapore, Australia, etc. |
| "You need to install Peppol software." | You use a **Peppol Access Point Provider**—no software installation required. |
| "Peppol replaces your ERP." | Peppol **integrates with** your ERP (e.g., Tally) via your Access Point. |
| "Peppol stores all your invoices." | Peppol is a **transmission network**—invoices are stored in your systems. |

---
### ## Summary: Peppol at a Glance

- **Network Type**: Open, standards-based, global e-document exchange network.
- **Model**: Four-corner (sender → sender AP → receiver AP → receiver).
- **Identifier**: Peppol ID (e.g., `urn:peppol:entity:iso6523-actorid-upin:<TRN>`).
- **Format**: UBL 2.1 XML (Peppol BIS Billing 3.0).
- **Governance**: OpenPeppol AISBL (global), FTA (UAE).
- **Access Points**: Certified providers (e.g., ClearTax, Spectra) handle routing and format conversion.
- **Use Case**: Mandatory e-invoicing in the UAE for VAT-registered businesses.

> **Final Note**: > The Peppol network is the **backbone of UAE e-invoicing**, enabling secure, automated, and compliant invoice exchange. Understanding its **four-corner model**, **Access Points**, and **Peppol ID** is essential for successful implementation.

## One-Pager: VAT on Commercial Property Sale (Hotel Apartment) – Non-Registered Seller

---

### **Background**
- A **Hotel Apartment** is classified as **commercial property** under **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017, Schedule 3**.
- The sale of commercial property is subject to **VAT at 5% standard rate** (Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, **Article 36**).
- A seller who is **not VAT-registered** and is making a one-time disposal does **not** need to obtain a **TRN**.
- VAT must be paid directly through the **FTA e-Services portal** under the dedicated **Non-Registered Persons** service before the ownership transfer process with the Land Department can proceed.

---

### **Step-by-Step Portal Process (Non-Registered Seller)**

1. **Create an e-Services Account**
   - Go to **[tax.gov.ae](https://tax.gov.ae)** → FTA e-Services portal.
   - Select **"Sign Up"** and complete registration:
     - Enter personal details (Emirates ID/Passport).
     - Verify email within **24 hours** (link expires after 24 hours).
     - Set username and password.

2. **Log In to FTA e-Services Portal**
   - After verification, log in using your credentials.
   - Complete alphanumeric verification if prompted.

3. **Navigate to VAT Payment**
   - Go to the **"My Payments"** tab.
   - Under **"Miscellaneous Payment"**, select:
     - **"Commercial Property Sale"** from the **"Payment for"** dropdown.

4. **Enter Mandatory Details**
   Fill in the following fields:
   - **Paying Entity Name (English & Arabic)**
   - **Property Details**:
     - Property Number
     - Date of Transaction
     - Land Department Transaction Number
     - Property Address
   - **Transaction Amount**: Enter sale price (e.g., AED 4,000,000).
   - **VAT Calculation**: System auto-computes **5%** (e.g., AED 200,000 for AED 4,000,000).

5. **Upload Required Documents**
   - Attach all mandatory files (see **Documents Required** below).

6. **Make Payment**
   - Click **"Make Payment"** → **"Pay Now"**.
   - Complete payment via:
     - **e-Dirham card**
     - **Credit card (Visa/MasterCard)**
     - **e-Dirham Instant**
   - **Save the Payment Transaction Number** (required for Land Department).

7. **Submit to Land Department**
   - Provide the **Payment Transaction Number** to the Land Department to proceed with ownership transfer.

---
### **Documents Required**
| Document | Details |
|---|---|
| **Sale/Transfer Agreement** | SPA or MOU (signed by both parties) |
| **Title Deed or Oqood** | Proof of ownership/registration |
| **Emirates ID or Passport** | Copy of seller’s ID (for verification) |
| **FTA Notice Copy** | SMS/email notification received from FTA |
| **VAT Calculation Worksheet** | Manual calculation of 5% VAT on sale price |
| **Land Department Transaction Number** | Unique identifier for the property transfer |

---
### **Legal References**
- **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017**, **Article 36** (VAT on commercial property sale).
- **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017**, **Schedule 3** (Hotel Apartment = commercial property).
- **FTA Public Clarification VATP015** (VAT on real estate transactions).
- **FTA VAT Payment User Guide for Commercial Property Buyers** (May 2021).

---
### **Key Notes**
- **No TRN is required** for a one-time disposal by a non-registered person.
- **VAT must be paid before ownership transfer** at the Land Department.
- **Payment Transaction Number** is mandatory for Land Department processing.
- The seller must report the output VAT in their **VAT return** (Box 1) to avoid double payment.

> **Pro-Tip:** Ensure all uploaded documents are clear and legible. Retain copies of the **Payment Transaction Number**, **payment receipt**, and **upload confirmation** for records. Delays in payment may halt the Land Department transfer process.

## VAT on Sale of Hotel Apartment by Non-Registered Person – In-Depth Explanation

---

### **1. Legal Classification & VAT Treatment**

#### **1.1 What is a Hotel Apartment?**
- A **Hotel Apartment** is explicitly classified as **commercial property** under **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017, Schedule 3**.
- This classification overrides any residential or mixed-use intent. Even if the unit is marketed as a "hotel apartment," it is treated as commercial property for VAT purposes.

#### **1.2 Why is VAT Applicable?**
- **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 36** states:
  > *"The supply of commercial property in the State shall be subject to VAT at the standard rate of 5%."*
- **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017, Schedule 3** confirms that **Hotel Apartments** fall under the definition of **commercial property**.
- Therefore, the sale of a hotel apartment is a **taxable supply** at **5% VAT**, regardless of whether the seller is registered or not.

#### **1.3 Who is Liable to Pay VAT?**
- **The seller** is legally responsible for charging and paying VAT to the FTA.
- **Non-registered sellers** do **not** need to register for VAT to make a one-time disposal.
- VAT must be **paid directly to the FTA** via the e-Services portal before the ownership transfer can be completed at the Land Department.

---

### **2. Step-by-Step Process (Detailed)**

#### **2.1 Step 1: Receive FTA Notice**
- The FTA typically sends a **SMS and email notification** to the seller (and sometimes the buyer) informing them of the VAT obligation.
- This notice includes:
  - Property details
  - Sale price
  - Suggested VAT amount
  - Deadline for payment
- **Keep this notice** — it is required for portal upload.

#### **2.2 Step 2: Register on FTA e-Services (If Not Already Registered)**
- Go to **[tax.gov.ae](https://tax.gov.ae)**
- Click **"Sign Up"** under **Non-Registered Persons**.
- Enter:
  - Full name (as per Emirates ID)
  - Emirates ID or Passport number
  - Mobile number and email
- Verify email within **24 hours** (link expires after 24 hours).
- Set username and password.
- Complete alphanumeric verification if prompted.

> **Pro-Tip:** Use a personal email (not work email) to avoid access issues later. Keep login credentials secure.

#### **2.3 Step 3: Log In and Navigate to Payment Service**
- Log in to **[tax.gov.ae](https://tax.gov.ae)**
- Go to **"My Payments"** → **"Miscellaneous Payment"**
- From the **"Payment for"** dropdown, select:
  > **"Commercial Property Sale"**
- This is a **dedicated service** for non-registered persons disposing of commercial property.

#### **2.4 Step 4: Enter Transaction Details**
Fill in the following fields accurately:

| Field | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|--------|
| **Paying Entity Name (English)** | Full name as per Emirates ID | Ahmed Ali Mohamed |
| **Paying Entity Name (Arabic)** | Full name in Arabic | أحمد علي محمد |
| **Property Number** | Unique identifier from Title Deed/Oqood | DLD-123456 |
| **Date of Transaction** | Date of sale agreement (SPA signing) | 15/05/2025 |
| **Land Department Transaction Number** | Unique number from DLD portal | LTRN-2025-001234 |
| **Property Address** | Full address including building and unit | Sheikh Zayed Road, Burj Khalifa Tower, Apartment 1201 |
| **Transaction Amount (AED)** | Total sale price | 4,000,000 |
| **VAT Amount (AED)** | Auto-calculated as 5% of sale price | 200,000 |

> **Note:** The system **automatically calculates 5% VAT** based on the sale price. Double-check the amount before proceeding.

#### **2.5 Step 5: Upload Required Documents**
All documents must be **clear, legible, and in PDF or JPEG format** (max 5MB per file).

| Document | Purpose | Tips |
|--------|--------|------|
| **Sale/Transfer Agreement (SPA or MOU)** | Proof of sale and agreed price | Must be signed by both parties |
| **Title Deed or Oqood** | Proof of ownership and property registration | Oqood = off-plan registration certificate |
| **Emirates ID or Passport Copy** | Identity verification of seller | Passport must have UAE entry stamp |
| **FTA Notice Copy** | Official notice received from FTA | SMS/email screenshot is acceptable |
| **VAT Calculation Worksheet** | Manual calculation showing 5% VAT | Include: Sale Price × 5% = VAT Due |
| **Land Department Transaction Number** | Confirmation of transfer request | Required to link payment to property |

> **Pro-Tip:** Name files clearly (e.g., "SPA_HotelApt_1201.pdf", "TitleDeed_1201.pdf") to avoid confusion during review.

#### **2.6 Step 6: Review and Submit**
- Review all entered data and uploaded documents.
- Confirm that:
  - Sale price matches SPA
  - VAT amount is correct (5%)
  - All documents are attached
- Click **"Submit"**

#### **2.7 Step 7: Make Payment**
- After submission, you’ll be redirected to the **payment gateway**.
- Accepted payment methods:
  - **e-Dirham card** (from UAE banks)
  - **Credit card** (Visa/MasterCard)
  - **e-Dirham Instant** (instant transfer)
- Payment is **instant** — no waiting period.
- Save the **Payment Transaction Number** (e.g., VAT-PAY-2025-00123456789).
  > This number is **mandatory** for the Land Department to process the ownership transfer.

#### **2.8 Step 8: Submit to Land Department**
- Provide the **Payment Transaction Number** to the Land Department (DLD or RERA portal).
- The transfer **cannot proceed** without this number.
- The seller must also **report this output VAT** in their **VAT return** (Box 1) to avoid double payment, even if not registered.

---

### **3. Legal & Regulatory Framework**

| Source | Reference | Key Point |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017** | **Article 36** | Supply of commercial property is taxable at 5% |
| **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017** | **Schedule 3** | Hotel Apartments = commercial property |
| **FTA Public Clarification** | **VATP015** | VAT on real estate transactions — confirms treatment of commercial property |
| **FTA VAT Payment User Guide** | May 2021 | Step-by-step portal instructions for non-registered persons |

> **Legal Note:** Failure to pay VAT before transfer may result in:
> - **Rejection of ownership transfer** by the Land Department
> - **Penalties** under Article 73 of the Decree-Law (late payment, non-payment)
> - **Legal action** for tax evasion

---

### **4. Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them**

| Pitfall | Risk | Solution |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Incorrect sale price entered** | Underpayment or overpayment of VAT | Cross-check SPA and Title Deed |
| **Missing FTA notice** | Payment rejected | Upload the SMS/email notification |
| **Wrong property number** | Delay in processing | Use exact number from Title Deed |
| **Not saving Payment Transaction Number** | Cannot complete land transfer | Save and share with DLD immediately |
| **Uploading low-quality documents** | Rejection by FTA | Use high-resolution scans or clear photos |
| **Paying after transfer date** | Penalties apply | Pay **before** signing transfer documents |

> **Warning:** The FTA **does not issue reminders**. It is the seller’s responsibility to comply within the deadline.

---

### **5. Deadlines & Compliance**

- **No fixed deadline** is published for one-time sales, but:
  - VAT must be paid **before the ownership transfer is registered**.
  - The Land Department **requires the Payment Transaction Number** before processing.
- **Penalties** (under Article 73):
  - **Late payment**: 4% monthly (capped at 36%)
  - **Non-payment**: AED 500–AED 50,000 fine
- **VAT Return Reporting**:
  - Even non-registered sellers must **report output VAT** in **Box 1** of their VAT return (if they file one).
  - This prevents double taxation and ensures compliance.

---

### **6. Partial Exemption Situations (Not Applicable Here)**
- **Partial exemption** applies when a business makes both **taxable and exempt supplies**.
- In this case:
  - The sale of a **single commercial property** is a **one-time taxable supply**.
  - There is **no input VAT recovery** involved.
  - Therefore, **partial exemption rules do not apply**.
- If the seller were a **VAT-registered business**, they would need to consider input VAT recovery on related costs, but this is **not relevant** for a one-time sale.

---

### **7. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)**

#### **Q: Do I need a TRN to pay VAT on this sale?**
A: **No.** Non-registered persons do **not** need a TRN for a one-time disposal. You can pay directly via the **Non-Registered Persons** service on the FTA portal.

#### **Q: Can the buyer pay the VAT instead?**
A: **No.** The **seller** is legally responsible for paying VAT. The FTA notice is issued to the seller, and the payment must come from them.

#### **Q: What if the sale price is AED 1,000,000 or less?**
A: **Still taxable at 5%.** There is **no threshold** for commercial property sales. Even small transactions are subject to VAT.

#### **Q: Can I claim input VAT on the purchase of the apartment?**
A: **Only if you are VAT-registered and used it for taxable business purposes.** For a one-time sale, input VAT recovery is **not applicable**.

#### **Q: What happens if I don’t pay VAT?**
A: The **Land Department will not process the transfer**. The FTA may issue penalties and pursue legal action.

---

### **8. Summary Checklist for Your Client**

✅ **Received FTA notice?** → Keep it.
✅ **Have SPA and Title Deed?** → Upload both.
✅ **Have Emirates ID/Passport?** → Copy ready.
✅ **Calculated 5% VAT?** → Double-check.
✅ **Created FTA e-Services account?** → Log in and proceed.
✅ **Uploaded all documents?** → Submit.
✅ **Made payment?** → Save **Payment Transaction Number**.
✅ **Shared number with Land Department?** → Transfer can proceed.

---
> **Final Note:** This is a **one-time transaction**, but compliance is **mandatory**. The FTA uses automated systems to detect non-compliance. Always act promptly to avoid penalties and delays in property transfer.

conversations.title: Client Received FTA Notice for Hotel Apartment VAT

messages.content: My client sold a Hotel Apartment and got FTA notice to pay VAT. Explain briefly.

## VAT on Sale of a Hotel Apartment (Commercial Property)

### Background
- A **Hotel Apartment** is classified as **commercial property** under **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017, Schedule 3**.
- The sale of commercial property is subject to **VAT at 5%** (Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, **Article 36**).
- The FTA notice you received indicates that the sale of the hotel apartment is a **taxable supply** and VAT must be accounted for.

### Key Points
- If your client is **not VAT-registered**, they are required to pay the **5% VAT** directly to the FTA via the e-Services portal before the ownership transfer can be completed.
- The buyer (or seller, depending on the agreement) must pay the VAT to the FTA and retain proof of payment to submit to the Land Department for ownership transfer.
- The VAT amount is calculated as **5% of the sale price** (e.g., AED 4,000,000 × 5% = AED 200,000).

### Steps to Comply
1. **Calculate VAT**: Compute **5%** of the sale price.
2. **Pay VAT via FTA Portal**:
   - Go to **tax.gov.ae** → FTA e-Services portal.
   - Select **Non-Registered Persons** → **"Payment of VAT on Commercial Property Sale"**.
   - Enter sale price, compute VAT, and complete payment.
3. **Retain Proof of Payment**: Obtain a **Payment Transaction Number** or proof of payment to submit to the Land Department for ownership transfer.

### Documents Required
- Sale/Transfer Agreement (SPA or MOU)
- Title Deed or Oqood
- Emirates ID or Passport copy
- Copy of FTA notice received
- VAT calculation worksheet

### Legal References
- **Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017**, **Article 36** (tax on commercial property sale)
- **Cabinet Decision No. 52 of 2017**, **Schedule 3** (Hotel Apartment = commercial property)
- **FTA Public Clarification VATP015** (VAT on real estate)

> **Pro-Tip:** Ensure VAT is paid **before** initiating the ownership transfer process with the Land Department to avoid delays. The Land Department will require proof of VAT payment (e.g., Payment Transaction Number) to proceed.

conversations.title: Client Received FTA VAT Notice After Hotel Apartment Sale

messages.content: My client sold a Hotel Apartment and got FTA notice to pay VAT. Explain and list required documents.

**VAT on Hotel Apartment Sale**

Based on the provided context, the sale of a hotel apartment is considered a commercial property sale, which is subject to 5% VAT (Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017).

**FTA Notice and VAT Payment**

The FTA notice received by your client indicates that the taxable supplies have reached the VAT registration threshold of AED 375,000. Your client is required to register for VAT within 10 business days of receiving the notification and send the VAT Tax Registration Number (TRN) to NonRegistered@tax.gov.ae.

**Required Documents for VAT Payment**

To complete the VAT payment, your client will need to create an e-Services account on the FTA website and provide the following documents:

1. **Emirates ID** and **Passport** of the buyer and seller
2. **Copy of Trade License** and **TRN certificate** of the seller
3. **TAX Invoice** for the supply of the property
4. **Mobile Number** and **Email ID** of the authorized person
5. **Property Details**:
	* Property Number
	* Date of Transaction
	* Land Department Transaction Number
	* Address of the property
6. **Proof of VAT Payment**:
	* Payment Transaction Number (received after paying VAT to FTA)
	* Proof of payment containing the details of the VAT payment (in case of bank payment)

**Steps for VAT Payment**

1. Create an e-Services account on the FTA website
2. Verify the e-Services account through email
3. Login to the FTA e-Services Portal and go to "MY PAYMENTS" tab
4. Select "Commercial Property Sale" from the "Payment for" drop-down list
5. Fill in the mandatory fields, including Land Department Transaction Number and property details
6. Pay the VAT due on the purchase directly to the FTA
7. Receive a Payment Transaction Number or proof of payment containing the details of the VAT payment
8. Produce the Payment Transaction Number or proof of payment to the Land Department to process the ownership transfer

**Note**: The seller will declare the output tax due on the property within its VAT return in the normal way and include the value of the output tax in the adjustment column of the return to avoid paying the output tax to the FTA twice.

conversations.title: VAT on Hotel Apartment Sales in UAE

messages.content: Briefly explain VAT on Hotel Apartment sale in UAE.

**VAT on Hotel Apartment Sales in UAE**

Hotel apartment sales in the UAE are subject to Value-Added Tax (VAT) under certain conditions. According to the UAE VAT law, the sale of hotel apartments is considered a taxable supply and is subject to 5% VAT (Source: vat treatment of properties Eng.pdf, Page 1).

However, if the hotel apartment is sold as a residential building, and the buyer is not a taxable person, the sale is exempt from VAT (Source: UAE-VAT-REAL-ESTATE-FAQ.pdf, Page 1).

Additionally, if the hotel apartment is sold as a commercial property, such as a serviced apartment, the sale is subject to 5% VAT (Source: Commercial Real Estate[1].docx, Page 1).

In cases where the hotel apartment is used for both residential and commercial purposes, the VAT treatment will depend on the primary use of the property (Source: Real Estate.pdf, Page 5).

**In summary:**

* Hotel apartment sales in the UAE are subject to 5% VAT if sold as a commercial property.
* Sales are exempt from VAT if sold as a residential building to a non-taxable person.
* VAT treatment depends on the primary use of the property if used for both residential and commercial purposes.

**References:**

* vat treatment of properties Eng.pdf
* UAE-VAT-REAL-ESTATE-FAQ.pdf
* Commercial Real Estate[1].docx
* Real Estate.pdf

messages.content: I have a client who sold Hotel Apartment and now got notice from FTA to pay VAT, need a one pager on this as well documents required to make payment on portal

## VAT Payment on Hotel Apartment Sale

### Overview

As per the UAE VAT law, the sale of commercial properties, including hotel apartments, is subject to 5% VAT. The buyer is required to pay the VAT directly to the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) before completing the ownership transfer process with the Land Department.

### Documents Required for VAT Payment on FTA Portal

To make the VAT payment on the FTA portal, the following documents are required:

*   Buyer's Emirates ID and Passport
*   Seller's Copy of Trade License and TRN certificate
*   TAX Invoice for the supply of this property
*   Mobile No and Email ID of the authorized person
*   Property Details:
    *   Property Number
    *   Date of Transaction
    *   Land Department Transaction Number
    *   Address of property

### Steps for VAT Payment on FTA Portal

1.  Create an e-Services account on the FTA portal
2.  Log in to the FTA portal and go to the 'My payments' tab
3.  Enter the details under 'Miscellaneous payment'
4.  Enter the mandatory details
5.  Make the VAT payment

### Important Notes

*   The buyer must pay the VAT directly to the FTA before completing the ownership transfer process with the Land Department.
*   The seller must issue a tax invoice to the buyer, but the buyer is responsible for paying the VAT to the FTA.
*   The buyer must produce the Payment Transaction Number or proof of payment to the Land Department to process the ownership transfer.

### References

*   VAT Payment for Commercial Property Buyers User Guide (Page 4)
*   Commercial Real Estate (Page 1)
*   Vat on Commercial Property (Page 1)
*   Purchase of Commercial Property - General (Page 1)
*   Real Estate (Page 19)
